references.authors: Nelson KM, Dahlin JL, Bisson J, et al.
references.title: The Essential Medicinal Chemistry of Curcumin.
references.finding: Argues curcumin is a PAINS/IMPS compound that is chemically unstable, reactive and not bioavailable; states that no double-blind placebo-controlled curcumin trial had been successful as of 2017.

references.authors: Nelson KM, Dahlin JL, Bisson J, et al.
references.title: Curcumin May (Not) Defy Science.
references.finding: The authors' follow-up reply to critics of their 2017 review, maintaining that curcumin is an improbable drug lead.

references.authors: Anand P, Nair HB, Sung B, et al.
references.title: Design of curcumin-loaded PLGA nanoparticles formulation with enhanced cellular uptake, and increased bioactivity in vitro and superior bioavailability in vivo.
references.finding: RETRACTED. Aggarwal-lab paper claiming PLGA-nanoparticle curcumin had superior bioactivity and bioavailability; cited here only as an example of the lab's retracted curcumin work.

references.authors: Yadav VR, Prasad S, Kannappan R, et al.
references.title: Cyclodextrin-complexed curcumin exhibits anti-inflammatory and antiproliferative activities superior to those of curcumin through higher cellular uptake.
references.finding: RETRACTED. Aggarwal-lab paper claiming cyclodextrin-complexed curcumin had superior anti-inflammatory activity in cell assays; cited only to flag the retraction.

references.authors: Poolsup N, Suksomboon N, Kurnianta PDM, et al.
references.title: Effects of curcumin on glycemic control and lipid profile in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: RETRACTED. A meta-analysis of curcumin on glycaemic control and lipids in prediabetes/type 2 diabetes; cited only to flag that it was withdrawn and should not be used.

references.authors: Schneider C, Gordon ON, Edwards RL, et al.
references.title: Degradation of Curcumin: From Mechanism to Biological Implications.
references.finding: Curcumin rapidly autoxidizes in vitro into many degradation products, which complicates interpretation of cell and animal data.

references.authors: Heger M, van Golen RF, Broekgaarden M, et al.
references.title: The molecular basis for the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of curcumin and its metabolites in relation to cancer.
references.finding: Detailed review of curcumin's chemistry (Michael acceptor, metal binding, photochemical instability), poor pharmacokinetics and metabolites in relation to cancer.

references.authors: Shoba G, Joy D, Joseph T, et al.
references.title: Influence of piperine on the pharmacokinetics of curcumin in animals and human volunteers.
references.finding: 2 g curcumin alone gave undetectable or very low serum levels; with 20 mg piperine bioavailability (AUC) rose about 2000%.

references.authors: Anand P, Kunnumakkara AB, Newman RA, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability of curcumin: problems and promises.
references.finding: Curcumin is tolerated up to 12 g/day but poorly bioavailable because of poor absorption, rapid metabolism and elimination (Aggarwal-lab review; not retracted).

references.authors: Lao CD, Ruffin MT 4th, Normolle D, et al.
references.title: Dose escalation of a curcuminoid formulation.
references.finding: Single doses of 0.5-12 g curcumin were well tolerated; no curcumin was detected in serum at 0.5-8 g and only low levels in two subjects at 10-12 g.

references.authors: Sharma RA, Euden SA, Platton SL, et al.
references.title: Phase I clinical trial of oral curcumin: biomarkers of systemic activity and compliance.
references.finding: Phase I, 0.45-3.6 g/day for up to 4 months: no dose-limiting toxicity; curcumin and conjugates in plasma only in the ~10 nmol/L range; 3.6 g lowered ex vivo inducible PGE2 in leukocytes.

references.authors: Cheng AL, Hsu CH, Lin JK, et al.
references.title: Phase I clinical trial of curcumin, a chemopreventive agent, in patients with high-risk or pre-malignant lesions.
references.finding: Phase I dose escalation from 0.5 to 12 g/day for 3 months found no toxicity up to 8 g/day for 3 months (higher doses were too bulky to take); mean peak serum curcumin was 0.51, 0.63 and 1.77 uM after 4, 6 and 8 g.

references.authors: Vareed SK, Kakarala M, Ruffin MT, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of curcumin conjugate metabolites in healthy human subjects.
references.finding: After 10 or 12 g curcumin, free curcumin was detectable in only one subject; glucuronide and sulfate conjugates were found in all (Cmax ~1.7-2.3 ug/mL).

references.authors: Garcea G, Berry DP, Jones DJ, et al.
references.title: Consumption of the putative chemopreventive agent curcumin by cancer patients: assessment of curcumin levels in the colorectum and their pharmacodynamic consequences.
references.finding: 3.6 g/day curcumin for 7 days gave colorectal tissue curcumin of ~8-13 nmol/g and lowered M1G DNA adducts in tissue: the gut wall is the one site where gram doses reach meaningful levels.

references.authors: Garcea G, Jones DJ, Singh R, et al.
references.title: Detection of curcumin and its metabolites in hepatic tissue and portal blood of patients following oral administration.
references.finding: 0.45-3.6 g/day curcumin for 1 week gave only low nanomolar parent and conjugates in portal and peripheral blood and no curcumin in liver tissue; oxidative DNA adducts in liver were not reduced.

references.authors: Cuomo J, Appendino G, Dern AS, et al.
references.title: Comparative absorption of a standardized curcuminoid mixture and its lecithin formulation.
references.finding: Phospholipid curcumin (Meriva) raised total curcuminoid absorption about 29-fold, but only phase-2 conjugates were detected and levels stayed below those needed for most anti-inflammatory targets.

references.authors: Jäger R, Lowery RP, Calvanese AV, et al.
references.title: Comparative absorption of curcumin formulations.
references.finding: Relative to standard curcumin, total curcuminoid exposure was 1.3-fold higher with turmeric-oil formulation, 7.9-fold with phytosome and 45.9-fold with a hydrophilic-carrier formulation (CHC).

references.authors: Schiborr C, Kocher A, Behnam D, et al.
references.title: The oral bioavailability of curcumin from micronized powder and liquid micelles is significantly increased in healthy humans and differs between sexes.
references.finding: Single 500 mg dose: micronized curcumin was 9-fold and liquid micellar curcumin 185-fold more bioavailable (AUC) than native powder; women absorbed more than men.

references.authors: Purpura M, Lowery RP, Wilson JM, et al.
references.title: Analysis of different innovative formulations of curcumin for improved relative oral bioavailability in human subjects.
references.finding: A gamma-cyclodextrin curcumin complex gave 39-fold higher total curcuminoid AUC than unformulated extract, exceeding a phytosome and a turmeric-oil formulation.

references.authors: Flory S, Sus N, Haas K, et al.
references.title: Increasing Post-Digestive Solubility of Curcumin Is the Most Successful Strategy to Improve its Oral Bioavailability: A Randomized Cross-Over Trial in Healthy Adults and In Vitro Bioaccessibility Experiments.
references.finding: Head-to-head test of 8 formulations at 207 mg curcumin: no free curcumin was detected in anyone; only micelles (57-fold) and gamma-cyclodextrin (30-fold) significantly raised conjugate AUC; piperine-type adjuvants did not.

references.authors: Stohs SJ, Chen CYO, Preuss HG, et al.
references.title: The fallacy of enzymatic hydrolysis for the determination of bioactive curcumin in plasma samples as an indication of bioavailability: a comparative study.
references.finding: Most curcumin PK studies hydrolyse plasma before analysis and so report total (free plus conjugated) curcumin, which overstates the bioactive free fraction.

references.authors: Luis PB, Kunihiro AG, Funk JL, et al.
references.title: Incomplete Hydrolysis of Curcumin Conjugates by β-Glucuronidase: Detection of Complex Conjugates in Plasma.
references.finding: Beta-glucuronidase only partly hydrolyses curcumin conjugates in plasma (complex sulfate conjugates remain), so 'total curcumin' assays differ by method and are hard to compare.

references.authors: Kanai M, Imaizumi A, Otsuka Y, et al.
references.title: Dose-escalation and pharmacokinetic study of nanoparticle curcumin, a potential anticancer agent with improved bioavailability, in healthy human volunteers.
references.finding: Theracurmin nanoparticle curcumin at 150 and 210 mg gave mean plasma Cmax of 189 and 275 ng/mL, without saturating absorption.

references.authors: Mahale J, Singh R, Howells LM, et al.
references.title: Detection of Plasma Curcuminoids from Dietary Intake of Turmeric-Containing Food in Human Volunteers.
references.finding: After a turmeric-containing meal at South Asian culinary levels, curcumin glucuronide peaked at ~48 nM and free curcumin was detectable (3.2 nM) in only one volunteer.

references.authors: Tayyem RF, Heath DD, Al-Delaimy WK, et al.
references.title: Curcumin content of turmeric and curry powders.
references.finding: HPLC of 28 spice products: pure turmeric powder averaged 3.14% curcumin by weight; most curry powders contained little and variable curcumin.

references.authors: Pal A, Sung B, Bhanu Prasad BA, et al.
references.title: Curcumin glucuronides: assessing the proliferative activity against human cell lines.
references.finding: Curcumin killed cancer cell lines at 1-10 uM, but its mono- and di-glucuronides (the main circulating forms) showed no antiproliferative activity.

references.authors: Kocher A, Bohnert L, Schiborr C, et al.
references.title: Highly bioavailable micellar curcuminoids accumulate in blood, are safe and do not reduce blood lipids and inflammation markers in moderately hyperlipidemic individuals.
references.finding: 294 mg/day micellar curcuminoids for 6 weeks reached fasting plasma ~49 nmol/L but did not change lipids, CRP or other inflammation markers versus placebo.

references.authors: Shin JW, Chun KS, Kim DH, et al.
references.title: Curcumin induces stabilization of Nrf2 protein through Keap1 cysteine modification.
references.finding: In mouse skin and epidermal cells, curcumin binds KEAP1 Cys151 and stabilises Nrf2 to induce HO-1; tetrahydrocurcumin, which lacks the Michael-acceptor group, does not.

references.authors: Balogun E, Hoque M, Gong P, et al.
references.title: Curcumin activates the haem oxygenase-1 gene via regulation of Nrf2 and the antioxidant-responsive element.
references.finding: In renal epithelial cells curcumin activates Nrf2 and induces haem oxygenase-1 through the antioxidant response element.

references.authors: Cheng D, Li W, Wang L, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and PKPD Modeling of Curcumin in Regulating Antioxidant and Epigenetic Gene Expression in Healthy Human Volunteers.
references.finding: After a single 4 g dose, parent curcumin was undetectable in plasma; curcumin glucuronide appeared and leukocyte NRF2/HO-1/NQO1 and HDAC mRNA changes were modelled as responses.

references.authors: Alvarenga L, Salarolli R, Cardozo LFMF, et al.
references.title: Impact of curcumin supplementation on expression of inflammatory transcription factors in hemodialysis patients: A pilot randomized, double-blind, controlled study.
references.finding: A juice containing 2.5 g turmeric three times weekly for 3 months lowered PBMC NF-kB mRNA and hs-CRP (3.8 to 2.0 mg/L) but did not change Nrf2 mRNA.

references.authors: Houghton CA, Fassett RG, Coombes JS
references.title: Sulforaphane and Other Nutrigenomic Nrf2 Activators: Can the Clinician's Expectation Be Matched by the Reality?
references.finding: Sulforaphane activates Nrf2 more potently and is far more bioavailable than curcumin, silymarin or resveratrol.

references.authors: Cheung KL, Khor TO, Kong AN
references.title: Synergistic effect of combination of phenethyl isothiocyanate and sulforaphane or curcumin and sulforaphane in the inhibition of inflammation.
references.finding: In cell culture, curcumin plus sulforaphane suppressed inflammatory markers (NO, PGE2, TNF, IL-1) synergistically, with synergistic HO-1 and NQO1 induction; no human data.

references.authors: Dinkova-Kostova AT, Talalay P
references.title: Direct and indirect antioxidant properties of inducers of cytoprotective proteins.
references.finding: Indirect antioxidants (Nrf2 inducers) act catalytically and durably through induced enzymes, unlike sacrificial direct antioxidants.

references.authors: Qin S, Huang L, Gong J, et al.
references.title: Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of 4 weeks or longer suggest that curcumin may afford some protection against oxidative stress.
references.finding: Curcumin >=4 weeks lowered MDA (SMD -0.77) and raised SOD (SMD 1.08) with no change in RBC GPx; the MDA effect appeared at >=600 mg/day curcuminoids.

references.authors: Jakubczyk K, Drużga A, Katarzyna J, et al.
references.title: Antioxidant Potential of Curcumin-A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
references.finding: Curcumin (mean 645 mg/day, ~67 days) raised total antioxidant capacity (SMD 2.70) and non-significantly lowered MDA (SMD -1.58, p=0.086); only four trials qualified.

references.authors: Dehzad MJ, Ghalandari H, Nouri M, et al.
references.title: Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of curcumin/turmeric supplementation in adults: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Turmeric/curcumin lowered CRP (-0.58 mg/L), TNF-a and IL-6 (-1.31 pg/mL), raised TAC (+0.21 mmol/L) and SOD, and lowered MDA (-0.33 umol/L); IL-1b unchanged.

references.authors: Kavyani Z, Najafi K, Naghsh N, et al.
references.title: The effects of curcumin supplementation on biomarkers of inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial function: A meta-analysis of meta-analyses.
references.finding: Umbrella analysis: curcumin lowered CRP (-0.87 mg/L), IL-6, TNF-a and MDA, raised SOD, GPx, catalase and FMD (+1.64%), but did not significantly change TAC.

references.authors: Ferguson JJA, Abbott KA, Garg ML
references.title: Anti-inflammatory effects of oral supplementation with curcumin: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Curcumin lowered CRP (-1.55 mg/L), IL-6 (-1.69 pg/mL) and TNF-a; authors note dose, duration and formulation remain unresolved.

references.authors: Lee YM, Kim Y
references.title: Is Curcumin Intake Really Effective for Chronic Inflammatory Metabolic Disease? A Review of Meta-Analyses of Randomized Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Review of meta-analyses: CRP fell in 7 of 10, IL-6 in 5 of 8, MDA in 5 of 6, fasting glucose in 14 of 15 and HOMA-IR in 12 of 12 meta-analyses of curcumin RCTs.

references.authors: Panahi Y, Hosseini MS, Khalili N, et al.
references.title: Antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of curcuminoid-piperine combination in subjects with metabolic syndrome: A randomized controlled trial and an updated meta-analysis.
references.finding: 1 g/day curcuminoids plus 10 mg piperine for 8 weeks raised SOD and lowered MDA and CRP versus placebo (Iranian trial, with an accompanying CRP meta-analysis).

references.authors: Wang Z, Singh A, Jones G, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and Safety of Turmeric Extracts for the Treatment of Knee Osteoarthritis: a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Turmeric extracts reduced knee OA pain (SMD -0.82) and improved function versus placebo, similar to NSAIDs; very high heterogeneity, moderate risk of bias, less benefit with higher BMI.

references.authors: Bannuru RR, Osani MC, Al-Eid F, et al.
references.title: Efficacy of curcumin and Boswellia for knee osteoarthritis: Systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Curcuminoids beat placebo for knee OA pain and function and matched NSAIDs with fewer GI adverse events, but study quality was low and most trials had <100 participants.

references.authors: Liu X, Machado GC, Eyles JP, et al.
references.title: Dietary supplements for treating osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Curcuma longa extract and curcumin were among 7 supplements with large short-term effects on OA pain, but no supplement showed clinically important long-term pain relief.

references.authors: Chen J, Zhou Q, Yu W, et al.
references.title: A critical review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses of curcumin for knee osteoarthritis.
references.finding: Overview of curcumin-for-knee-OA reviews: methodological quality extremely low, heavy overlap, and 37 of 48 outcomes rated extremely low-quality evidence.

references.authors: Wang Z, Jones G, Winzenberg T, et al.
references.title: Effectiveness of Curcuma longa Extract for the Treatment of Symptoms and Effusion-Synovitis of Knee Osteoarthritis : A Randomized Trial.
references.n: 70 adults with knee OA and effusion-synovitis
references.finding: Curcuma longa extract (2 capsules/day, 12 weeks) cut VAS knee pain by 9.1 mm versus placebo but did not change effusion-synovitis volume or cartilage; funded partly by the manufacturer.

references.authors: Kuptniratsaikul V, Dajpratham P, Taechaarpornkul W, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and safety of Curcuma domestica extracts compared with ibuprofen in patients with knee osteoarthritis: a multicenter study.
references.finding: Curcuma domestica extract 1500 mg/day was non-inferior to ibuprofen 1200 mg/day over 4 weeks on WOMAC, with fewer abdominal complaints.

references.authors: Nakagawa Y, Mukai S, Yamada S, et al.
references.title: Short-term effects of highly-bioavailable curcumin for treating knee osteoarthritis: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled prospective study.
references.finding: Theracurmin (180 mg/day curcumin) for 8 weeks lowered knee-pain VAS versus placebo (except in mild cases) and reduced celecoxib use; developer-affiliated study.

references.authors: Belcaro G, Cesarone MR, Dugall M, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and safety of Meriva®, a curcumin-phosphatidylcholine complex, during extended administration in osteoarthritis patients.
references.finding: Meriva for 8 months improved WOMAC scores and inflammatory markers versus a control group; open, non-randomised design.

references.authors: Musso G, Pinach S, Mariano F, et al.
references.title: Effect of phospholipid curcumin Meriva on liver histology and kidney disease in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
references.finding: Meriva 2 g/day for 72 weeks: NASH resolution in 62% vs 12% on placebo and fibrosis improvement in 50% vs 8%; single trial, needs replication.

references.authors: Vajdi M, Hassanizadeh S, Hassanizadeh R, et al.
references.title: Curcumin supplementation effect on liver enzymes in patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: In NAFLD, curcumin lowered ALT (-4.1 U/L) and AST (-3.3 U/L) but not ALP; curcumin plus piperine had no significant effect on ALT.

references.authors: Ebrahimzadeh A, Mohseni S, Safargar M, et al.
references.title: Curcumin effects on glycaemic indices, lipid profile, blood pressure, inflammatory markers and anthropometric measurements of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
references.finding: In NAFLD, curcumin 50-3000 mg/day lowered fasting glucose, HOMA-IR, TG, TC, LDL and weight but not HbA1c, CRP, TNF-a or blood pressure; authors flag bias and possible adulteration.

references.authors: Bahari H, Jazinaki MS, Asadi Z, et al.
references.title: Curcumin/Turmeric Supplementation on Glycemic Control in Adults With Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: In prediabetes/type 2 diabetes, curcumin/turmeric lowered fasting glucose (-10.2 mg/dL), HbA1c (-0.32%) and HOMA-IR, with larger effects at >=1 g/day; heterogeneity was substantial.

references.authors: Chuengsamarn S, Rattanamongkolgul S, Luechapudiporn R, et al.
references.title: Curcumin extract for prevention of type 2 diabetes.
references.finding: 9 months of curcumin extract: 0% vs 16.4% progressed to type 2 diabetes, with better HOMA-beta and HOMA-IR; an unusually large single-trial effect not yet replicated.

references.authors: Funamoto M, Shimizu K, Sunagawa Y, et al.
references.title: Effects of Highly Absorbable Curcumin in Patients with Impaired Glucose Tolerance and Non-Insulin-Dependent Diabetes Mellitus.
references.finding: Theracurmin 180 mg/day for 6 months did not change HbA1c (primary endpoint); oxidised LDL rose in the placebo group but not with curcumin.

references.authors: Altobelli E, Angeletti PM, Marziliano C, et al.
references.title: Potential Therapeutic Effects of Curcumin on Glycemic and Lipid Profile in Uncomplicated Type 2 Diabetes-A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trial.
references.finding: Curcumin did not significantly lower fasting glucose but did reduce HbA1c, HOMA and LDL in uncomplicated type 2 diabetes.

references.authors: Dehzad MJ, Ghalandari H, Amini MR, et al.
references.title: Effects of curcumin/turmeric supplementation on lipid profile: A GRADE-assessed systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Turmeric/curcumin lowered TC (-4.0 mg/dL), TG (-6.7), LDL (-4.9) and raised HDL (+1.8) but did not change ApoA or ApoB; GRADE certainty low to very low.

references.authors: Sahebkar A
references.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials investigating the effects of curcumin on blood lipid levels.
references.finding: Early meta-analysis found no significant effect of curcumin on any blood lipid.

references.authors: Ng QX, Koh SSH, Chan HW, et al.
references.title: Clinical Use of Curcumin in Depression: A Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Curcumin improved Hamilton depression scores versus placebo (SMD -0.34); few, small trials.

references.authors: Musazadeh V, Faghfouri AH, Falahatzadeh M, et al.
references.title: Efficacy of curcumin in depression: A grade-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Curcumin improved depression (SMD -0.76) and depressive symptoms (SMD -0.53) but heterogeneity was very high (I2 >85%) and the effect was fragile in sensitivity analysis.

references.authors: Cheng YC, Huang WL, Chen WY, et al.
references.title: Comparative efficacy and tolerability of nutraceuticals for depressive disorder: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
references.finding: Network meta-analysis: curcumin added to antidepressants improved symptoms (SMD 1.03), while curcumin monotherapy versus antidepressants was not significant (CI crossed zero).

references.authors: Small GW, Siddarth P, Li Z, et al.
references.title: Memory and Brain Amyloid and Tau Effects of a Bioavailable Form of Curcumin in Non-Demented Adults: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled 18-Month Trial.
references.finding: Theracurmin 90 mg curcumin twice daily for 18 months improved verbal and visual memory and attention versus placebo and lowered FDDNP-PET signal in amygdala/hypothalamus; very small trial.

references.authors: Ringman JM, Frautschy SA, Teng E, et al.
references.title: Oral curcumin for Alzheimer's disease: tolerability and efficacy in a 24-week randomized, double blind, placebo-controlled study.
references.finding: Curcumin C3 Complex 2 or 4 g/day for 24 weeks showed no clinical or biomarker benefit; native plasma curcumin was low (7.3 ng/mL) and 3 withdrew for GI symptoms.

references.authors: Rainey-Smith SR, Brown BM, Sohrabi HR, et al.
references.title: Curcumin and cognition: a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind study of community-dwelling older adults.
references.finding: Biocurcumax 1500 mg/day for 12 months: no difference on most cognitive measures; one MoCA interaction driven by decline in the placebo group at 6 months.

references.authors: Cox KH, Pipingas A, Scholey AB
references.title: Investigation of the effects of solid lipid curcumin on cognition and mood in a healthy older population.
references.finding: Longvida solid-lipid curcumin 400 mg improved attention and working memory acutely and after 4 weeks, and lowered total and LDL cholesterol.

references.authors: Wang W, Zhao R, Liu B, et al.
references.title: The effect of curcumin supplementation on cognitive function: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
references.finding: Curcumin improved global cognition (SMD 0.82) only in trials >=24 weeks, in people >=60 or in Asian populations; small evidence base.

references.authors: Ng TP, Chiam PC, Lee T, et al.
references.title: Curry consumption and cognitive function in the elderly.
references.finding: Occasional or frequent curry eaters had better MMSE scores than never/rare eaters (cross-sectional association, confounding possible).

references.authors: Fang W, Nasir Y
references.title: The effect of curcumin supplementation on recovery following exercise-induced muscle damage and delayed-onset muscle soreness: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
references.finding: Curcumin lowered creatine kinase (-48.5 IU/L) and muscle-soreness scores (WMD -0.48) after damaging exercise.

references.authors: Liu X, Lin L, Hu G
references.title: Meta-analysis of the effect of curcumin supplementation on skeletal muscle damage status.
references.finding: Curcumin reduced muscle soreness (MD -0.61), CK (MD -137) and IL-6 and improved range of motion after exercise.

references.authors: Bańkowski S, Petr M, Rozpara M, et al.
references.title: Effect of 6-week curcumin supplementation on aerobic capacity, antioxidant status and sirtuin 3 level in middle-aged amateur long-distance runners.
references.finding: 2 g/day curcumin for 6 weeks did not change VO2max, antioxidant enzymes, oxidative-stress or muscle-damage markers; resting SIRT3 rose.

references.authors: Ray Hamidie RD, Yamada T, Ishizawa R, et al.
references.title: Curcumin treatment enhances the effect of exercise on mitochondrial biogenesis in skeletal muscle by increasing cAMP levels.
references.finding: In rats, injected curcumin plus endurance training increased muscle mitochondrial biogenesis markers more than training alone (via cAMP/PKA, AMPK/PGC-1a).

references.authors: Ristow M, Zarse K, Oberbach A, et al.
references.title: Antioxidants prevent health-promoting effects of physical exercise in humans.
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Vitamin C 1000 mg plus vitamin E 400 IU/day blocked exercise-induced gains in insulin sensitivity and induction of endogenous antioxidant defences.

references.authors: Gomez-Cabrera MC, Domenech E, Romagnoli M, et al.
references.title: Oral administration of vitamin C decreases muscle mitochondrial biogenesis and hampers training-induced adaptations in endurance performance.
references.finding: 1 g/day vitamin C reduced training-induced mitochondrial biogenesis and endurance adaptations.

references.authors: Cruz-Correa M, Hylind LM, Marrero JH, et al.
references.title: Efficacy and Safety of Curcumin in Treatment of Intestinal Adenomas in Patients With Familial Adenomatous Polyposis.
references.finding: Pure curcumin 3 g/day for 12 months did not reduce the number or size of intestinal adenomas versus placebo.

references.authors: Carroll RE, Benya RV, Turgeon DK, et al.
references.title: Phase IIa clinical trial of curcumin for the prevention of colorectal neoplasia.
references.finding: Curcumin 4 g/day (not 2 g) for 30 days cut aberrant crypt foci by 40%, but did not change PGE2, 5-HETE or Ki-67; non-randomised.

references.authors: Howells LM, Iwuji COO, Irving GRB, et al.
references.title: Curcumin Combined with FOLFOX Chemotherapy Is Safe and Tolerable in Patients with Metastatic Colorectal Cancer in a Randomized Phase IIa Trial.
references.finding: Adding 2 g/day curcumin to FOLFOX was safe; exploratory overall-survival HR 0.34 in an open-label phase IIa trial too small for efficacy conclusions.

references.authors: Ryan Wolf J, Heckler CE, Guido JJ, et al.
references.title: Oral curcumin for radiation dermatitis: a URCC NCORP study of 686 breast cancer patients.
references.finding: Oral curcumin 6 g/day during radiotherapy did not reduce radiation dermatitis severity versus placebo.

references.authors: Choi YH, Han DH, Kim SW, et al.
references.title: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the role of curcumin in prostate cancer patients with intermittent androgen deprivation.
references.n: 97 men with prostate cancer on intermittent ADT
references.finding: Curcumin 1440 mg/day for 6 months did not lengthen the off-treatment interval versus placebo.

references.authors: Dhillon N, Aggarwal BB, Newman RA, et al.
references.title: Phase II trial of curcumin in patients with advanced pancreatic cancer.
references.finding: 8 g/day curcumin: low circulating conjugates, 2 of 21 evaluable patients showed biological activity; uncontrolled phase II.

references.authors: Alizadeh F, Javadi M, Karami AA, et al.
references.title: Curcumin nanomicelle improves semen parameters, oxidative stress, inflammatory biomarkers, and reproductive hormones in infertile men: A randomized clinical trial.
references.finding: 80 mg/day curcumin nanomicelle for 10 weeks raised sperm count, concentration and motility and improved TAC, MDA, CRP and TNF-a versus placebo; single small Iranian trial, no pregnancy or DNA-fragmentation outcomes.

references.authors: Naz RK
references.title: Can curcumin provide an ideal contraceptive?
references.finding: Curcumin added to human and mouse sperm caused concentration-dependent loss of forward motility, capacitation and fertilisation in vitro, and intravaginal curcumin reduced fertility in mice.

references.authors: Santonastaso M, Mottola F, Iovine C, et al.
references.title: Protective Effects of Curcumin on the Outcome of Cryopreservation in Human Sperm.
references.finding: Adding 20 uM curcumin to freezing medium improved post-thaw motility and lowered ROS and DNA fragmentation in human sperm (in vitro, cryopreservation only).

references.authors: Sadraei MR, Tavalaee M, Forouzanfar M, et al.
references.title: Effect of curcumin, and nano-curcumin on sperm function in varicocele rat model.
references.finding: In varicocele rats, oral curcumin and nano-curcumin improved sperm concentration, motility, lipid peroxidation and DNA damage.

references.authors: Abdelazeem B, Abbas KS, Shehata J, et al.
references.title: The effects of curcumin as dietary supplement for patients with polycystic ovary syndrome: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials.
references.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.55) and total cholesterol, with no effect on LDL, HDL, sex hormones, weight or CRP.

references.authors: Chien YJ, Chang CY, Wu MY, et al.
references.title: Effects of Curcumin on Glycemic Control and Lipid Profile in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis and Trial Sequential Analysis.
references.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (-0.32), HDL and total cholesterol but not LDL or triglycerides.

references.authors: Simental-Mendía LE, Shah N, Sathyapalan T, et al.
references.title: Effect of Curcumin on Glycaemic and Lipid Parameters in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
references.finding: Curcumin lowered fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin and HOMA-IR (-0.94, I2 90%) but did not change any lipid index.

references.authors: Mohammadi S, Ziaei S, Morvaridi M, et al.
references.title: Impacts of Curcumin Supplementation on Cardiometabolic Risk Factors in Patients With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
references.finding: Curcumin modestly lowered fasting glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR (SMD -0.36) and TC, but did not change BMI, testosterone, DHEA, LH or FSH.

references.authors: Feghhi F, Ghaznavi H, Sheervalilou R, et al.
references.title: Effects of metformin and curcumin in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: A factorial clinical trial.
references.finding: Nanocurcumin 80 mg three times daily plus metformin improved lipids, glucose markers, weight and testosterone more than either agent alone or placebo over 12 weeks.

references.authors: Ghanbarzadeh-Ghashti N, Ghanbari-Homaie S, Shaseb E, et al.
references.title: The effect of Curcumin on metabolic parameters and androgen level in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: 1000 mg/day curcumin for 12 weeks lowered fasting glucose and reduced amenorrhoea/oligomenorrhoea (13% vs 22%) versus placebo, but did not change lipids, insulin, SHBG, testosterone or hirsutism.

references.authors: Jannatifar R, Asa E, Cheraghi E, et al.
references.title: Nanomicelle curcumin improves oxidative stress, inflammatory markers, and assisted reproductive techniques outcomes in endometriosis cases: a randomized clinical trial.
references.n: 50 women with stage III/IV endometriosis undergoing ART
references.finding: Nanomicelle curcumin 120 mg/day for 10 weeks improved serum and follicular-fluid oxidative-stress markers and reported more oocytes, mature oocytes and good embryos; small single-centre trial.

references.authors: Gudarzi R, Shabani F, Mohammad-Alizadeh-Charandabi S, et al.
references.title: Effect of curcumin on painful symptoms of endometriosis: A triple-blind randomized controlled trial.
references.finding: Curcumin 1000 mg/day for 8 weeks did not improve endometriosis pain or quality of life versus placebo.

references.authors: Chen CC, Chan WH
references.title: Injurious effects of curcumin on maturation of mouse oocytes, fertilization and fetal development via apoptosis.
references.finding: In mice, curcumin (in vitro and 40 uM in drinking water) impaired oocyte maturation, fertilisation and early embryo development via apoptosis.

references.authors: Azami SH, Nazarian H, Abdollahifar MA, et al.
references.title: The antioxidant curcumin postpones ovarian aging in young and middle-aged mice.
references.finding: In mice, intraperitoneal curcumin (100 mg/kg/day) preserved follicle numbers, AMH and oocyte quality with age.

references.authors: Lombardi N, Crescioli G, Maggini V, et al.
references.title: Acute liver injury following turmeric use in Tuscany: An analysis of the Italian Phytovigilance database and systematic review of case reports.
references.finding: Italian phytovigilance cases of acute (mostly cholestatic) hepatitis were all linked to high-bioavailability, high-dose curcumin products; positive dechallenge in most.

references.authors: Menniti-Ippolito F, Ippoliti I, Pastorelli AA, et al.
references.title: Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) food supplements and hepatotoxicity: an integrated evaluation approach.
references.finding: A 2019 Italian cluster of 28 acute hepatitis reports linked to turmeric supplements; product testing looked for drugs, metals, aflatoxins, dyes and pyrrolizidine alkaloids, and regulators intervened.

references.authors: Halegoua-DeMarzio D, Navarro V, Ahmad J, et al.
references.title: Liver Injury Associated with Turmeric-A Growing Problem: Ten Cases from the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network [DILIN].
references.finding: US DILIN turmeric liver-injury cases rose since 2011; typically hepatocellular after 1-4 months, one death, 3 of 7 tested products contained piperine, and 7 of 10 patients carried HLA-B*35:01.

references.authors: Bahramsoltani R, Rahimi R, Farzaei MH
references.title: Pharmacokinetic interactions of curcuminoids with conventional drugs: A review.
references.finding: Curcumin inhibits CYP isoenzymes and P-glycoprotein and alters drug pharmacokinetics in vitro and in animals; human interaction data are sparse.

references.authors: Hu S, Belcaro G, Dugall M, et al.
references.title: Interaction study between antiplatelet agents, anticoagulants, thyroid replacement therapy and a bioavailable formulation of curcumin (Meriva®).
references.n: patients on antiplatelets, anticoagulants, levothyroxine or metformin
references.finding: 10-15 days of Meriva did not change bleeding time on aspirin/clopidogrel/ticlopidine, INR on warfarin or dabigatran, thyroid tests or glycaemia; short, uncontrolled, sponsor-linked.

references.authors: Liu AC, Zhao LX, Lou HX
references.title: Curcumin alters the pharmacokinetics of warfarin and clopidogrel in Wistar rats but has no effect on anticoagulation or antiplatelet aggregation.
references.finding: In rats, 100 mg/kg curcumin raised warfarin and clopidogrel exposure (~1.5-1.8-fold) without changing prothrombin time or platelet aggregation.

references.authors: Kusuhara H, Furuie H, Inano A, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetic interaction study of sulphasalazine in healthy subjects and the impact of curcumin as an in vivo inhibitor of BCRP.
references.finding: 2 g curcumin inhibited intestinal BCRP and raised sulfasalazine exposure 2.0-3.2-fold in humans.

references.authors: Pattanaik S, Hota D, Prabhakar S, et al.
references.title: Effect of piperine on the steady-state pharmacokinetics of phenytoin in patients with epilepsy.
references.finding: A single 20 mg piperine dose significantly raised phenytoin AUC and Cmax at steady state.

references.authors: Tuntipopipat S, Judprasong K, Zeder C, et al.
references.title: Chili, but not turmeric, inhibits iron absorption in young women from an iron-fortified composite meal.
references.finding: 0.5 g turmeric in a meal did not inhibit iron absorption (stable isotopes), whereas chili cut it by 38%.

references.authors: Jiao Y, Wilkinson J 4th, Di X, et al.
references.title: Curcumin, a cancer chemopreventive and chemotherapeutic agent, is a biologically active iron chelator.
references.finding: In mice with marginal iron intake, dietary curcumin acted as an iron chelator, lowered hepcidin and caused iron-deficiency anaemia.

references.authors: Rasyid A, Rahman AR, Jaalam K, et al.
references.title: Effect of different curcumin dosages on human gall bladder.
references.finding: Curcumin 20, 40 and 80 mg contracted the gallbladder by 34%, 51% and 72% within 2 h.

references.authors: Tang M, Larson-Meyer DE, Liebman M
references.title: Effect of cinnamon and turmeric on urinary oxalate excretion, plasma lipids, and plasma glucose in healthy subjects.
references.finding: Supplemental turmeric raised urinary oxalate excretion (91% of its oxalate is soluble) and did not change glucose or lipids over 4 weeks.

references.authors: Forsyth JE, Nurunnahar S, Islam SS, et al.
references.title: Turmeric means "yellow" in Bengali: Lead chromate pigments added to turmeric threaten public health across Bangladesh.
references.finding: Lead chromate pigment (2-10% lead by weight) is added to turmeric during polishing in 7 of 9 major producing districts of Bangladesh to meet demand for bright yellow colour.

references.authors: Forsyth JE, Mistree D, Nash E, et al.
references.title: Evidence of turmeric adulteration with lead chromate across South Asia.
references.finding: 14% of turmeric samples from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal had detectable lead (>2 ug/g); some exceeded 1000 ug/g with 1:1 lead:chromium ratios indicating lead chromate.

references.authors: Cowell W, Ireland T, Vorhees D, et al.
references.title: Ground Turmeric as a Source of Lead Exposure in the United States.
references.finding: Describes US childhood lead-poisoning cases traced to spices; all 32 turmeric samples bought in Boston contained lead (0.03-99.5 ppm), half above the FDA candy limit of 0.1 ppm.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS)
references.title: Scientific Opinion on the re-evaluation of curcumin (E 100) as a food additive.
references.finding: Set an ADI of 3 mg/kg bw/day for curcumin, from a NOAEL of 250-320 mg/kg bw/day (lower F2 body-weight gain in a reproductive toxicity study) with a 100-fold uncertainty factor; not carcinogenic or genotoxic.

references.authors: US National Library of Medicine
references.title: PubMed searches 'Aggarwal BB[au] AND retracted publication[pt]' and 'curcumin AND retracted publication[pt]', run 2026-10-01 via NCBI E-utilities.
references.finding: Returned 27 retracted publications with BB Aggarwal as author and 162 retracted publications mentioning curcumin.
